demo_clock: Sample Monday on an America/New_York demo clock. Moving a source's time of day onto it is a relabelling, not a timezone conversion.
summary: Busyness at BU-named places is simulated. FitRec follows one recorded day at a real campus gym elsewhere; Mugar Library follows people counts from one small library room in Singapore; dining halls follow canteen purchases in Switzerland at lunch, turned into diners by an assumed meal length, with breakfast and dinner modeled. All of it is rescaled to illustrative sizes. None of it measures BU.
measures_note: ROBOD counts people in a room. NOVANIMAL records purchases (checkouts), not people present: turning them into diners needs an assumed meal length, so the dining values are a model driven by real purchase times.

datasets.paper: Tekler, Z.D., Ono, E., Peng, Y., Zhang, S., Lasternas, B., Chong, A. (2022). ROBOD, room-level occupancy and building operation dataset. Building Simulation. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12273-022-0925-9
datasets.original_location: Room 5, a library space in the SDE4 building, National University of Singapore (not BU)
datasets.metric: occupant_count [number]: people in the room (ground truth), 0-16
datasets.sampling: every 5 minutes on 47 recorded weekdays, 2021-09-07 to 2021-12-23, with gaps between periods
datasets.timezone: local time with a +08:00 UTC offset (Singapore), kept as written
datasets.measurement: Ground-truth occupant counts collected with the room's sensor data (publisher's description). Wi-Fi device counts and the presence flag are not used.

datasets.title: NOVANIMAL aggregated menu sales (ZHAW canteens, autumn 2017)
datasets.obligations: Attribute the creator and the working paper; indicate changes.
datasets.citation: Supplementary material (aggregated data set): Egeler, G.-A. & Baur, P. (2020). Menüwahl in der Hochschulmensa: Fleisch oder Vegi? Ergebnisse eines 12-wöchigen Feldexperiments (NOVANIMAL Working Paper No. 5). ZHAW. https://doi.org/10.21256/zhaw-1405
datasets.paper: Egeler, G.-A. & Baur, P. (2020). NOVANIMAL Working Paper No. 5. ZHAW. https://doi.org/10.21256/zhaw-1405
datasets.original_location: Two ZHAW university canteens, Grüental and Vista (Wädenswil, Switzerland), not BU
datasets.metric: Point-of-sale transactions (purchases), grouped from article lines; not people
datasets.sampling: every sale, 2017-10-02 to 2017-12-22 (60 weekdays), almost all at lunch
datasets.timezone: trans_date ends in 'Z' but is read as local wall-clock time: the publisher's variable list shows it without a zone and sale times don't move when Swiss summer time ends (see data/novanimal_quality.md)
datasets.measurement: Canteen till records. A transaction can include several menus or a weighed buffet plate; qty_weight (menus or kg) is never used as people.
datasets.modifications: 26,340 article lines grouped into 25,627 purchases (one refund left out), counted per 15 minutes, turned into illustrative diners and rescaled (see the dining simulation). The original is unchanged in data/raw/novanimal/.
datasets.notes: The individual data set (doi:10.5281/zenodo.3890949) is more personally detailed and isn't used.

datasets.title: Room Occupancy Estimation
datasets.original_location: One 6 m x 4.6 m test room (controlled experiment)
datasets.metric: Room_Occupancy_Count: 0-3 people, noted manually as ground truth
datasets.sampling: every ~30 s; 2017-12-22 to 2018-01-11 with a 15-day gap
datasets.measurement: Manual ground truth alongside environmental sensors.
datasets.notes: Not used for dining: people were present on only three days, on an experimenter-chosen schedule of 0-3 people. Shaping that into meal times would make the model, not the data, decide the curve, so citing it would mislead.

simulations.label: Simulated from a real campus gym (not BU)
simulations.source_period: 2016-12-05, a Monday (-08:00), the gym's default playback day
simulations.gap_handling: Latest reading at or before each slot if at most 30 minutes old; otherwise the slot stays empty.
transformations: Take the gym's readings for 2016-12-05 (source local time, offset kept in the source file).
Every 15 minutes from 6:00 to 24:00 (FitRec's sample hours), take the latest reading at or before that time if it is at most 30 minutes old; otherwise leave the slot empty (never zero).
Place each slot at the same clock time on the demo Monday (a relabelling, not a timezone conversion).
Multiply by 9.0625: the gym's typical high (72 people, its 95% time-weighted percentile) becomes 75% of FitRec's illustrative capacity (870). Round to whole people.
assumptions: FitRec's time-of-day pattern resembles this gym's on one in-semester Monday.
The scale is a design choice for the demo, not FitRec's real size or capacity.
limits: One count for the whole building, not a measurement of FitRec: it can't say which court, pool or room is in use, and no queue, equipment or court availability can be read from it.
One source day: it shows a plausible pattern, not BU's typical traffic or a forecast.
The source gym's counting method isn't documented.

simulations.label: Simulated from a library room's counts (not BU)

periods.label: Not simulated: the source library room is empty by this hour

simulations.metric: people present in one room (source) → people present in the building (simulated)
simulations.gap_handling: Each reading stands for 5 minutes (the cadence) and never past local midnight; gaps between recorded periods are no data.
transformations: Take Room 5's occupant_count on every recorded Monday (9 days), in source local time with its +08:00 offset.
For each 15-minute slot, take the time-weighted mean count (each reading stands for 5 minutes), then average that slot over the 9 days.
Keep only 08:00-22:00: within Mugar's sample hours and the hours when someone was in the room on at least one recorded Monday (08:00-22:00).
Place each slot at the same clock time on the demo Monday (a relabelling, not a timezone conversion).

Multiply by 45.0: the room's typical high (10 people, its 95% time-weighted percentile over 08:00-22:00 on all 47 recorded dates) becomes 75% of Mugar's illustrative capacity (600). Round to whole people.
assumptions: Mugar's time-of-day pattern resembles this one library room's average weekday pattern.
The scale is a design choice for the demo: ROBOD measures a small room (at most 16 people), and neither its maximum nor the scale says anything about Mugar's real size or capacity.
limits: One small room in Singapore stands in for a large building in Boston: a pattern, not a measurement.
Averaging several days smooths the curve; the dates include later-semester weeks with lower use.

No values 22:00-24:00, though Mugar's sample hours run later: the room is empty by then on every recorded Monday, which says nothing about a library open late. Shown as no data, not as zero or closed.
No seat or quiet-space availability can be read from it.

simulations.label: Lunch simulated from canteen sales (not BU); other hours modeled

targets.name: Fenway Dining
targets.hours: no sample hours; simulated 07:00-23:00 like the other halls

simulations.source_period: all 24 canteen-Mondays (2 canteens x 12 Mondays, 2017-10-02 to 2017-12-18), source wall clock
simulations.metric: purchases per 15 minutes (source) → illustrative diners present (simulated)
simulations.gap_handling: A 15-minute interval the source doesn't list counts as no purchases (the canteen recorded none); lunch is the only period the source supports.
transformations: Group article lines into purchases by (canteen, date, transaction_id); a purchase counts once whatever it contains (import step).
Count purchases per 15 minutes on the source wall clock.
Lunch window 11:00-13:30: the 15-minute-aligned span holding the central 99.5% of all purchases.
Illustrative diners at a time = purchases in the 30 minutes before it (each purchase stands for one diner for 30 minutes), so lunch values run 11:00-14:00.
Average each slot over all 24 canteen-Mondays (both canteens pooled).
Per hall, multiply by 0.75 x illustrative capacity / 103 (the 95% percentile of diners over every canteen-day and lunch slot), so a typical high becomes the busy threshold. Round to whole people.
Outside 11:00-14:00, use the modeled breakfast and evening knots x illustrative capacity. Each slot comes from exactly one period: no blending, nothing counted twice.
assumptions: Meal length: each purchase is one diner present for 30 minutes. Illustrative, not measured.
One purchase is one diner. A purchase can be for several people, and people who don't buy (or bring food) aren't counted.
BU halls share one lunch shape; their differences come only from illustrative capacities.
Breakfast and dinner levels are a modeling choice, not evidence: NOVANIMAL covers lunch only.
limits: Purchases are not occupancy: the source records checkouts, not arrivals, departures or seats.
No wait times, queues, table or seat availability can be read from it.
Two Swiss canteens in 2017 stand in for four BU dining halls: a pattern, not a measurement.

illustrative: Capacities (FitRec, dining halls, Mugar) and the busyness thresholds (quiet under 40%, busy from 75%).
The scale factors and the 30-minute meal length.
Opening hours, the FitRec amenity list and study amenities.
Walking times between demo locations (not routed).
The demo Monday and its clock.
